Features: [...] ### Holafly reviews

Holafly on Trustpilot: 4.6/5 star rating. About 85% of views are 5-star. They also have a whopping 65,000+ reviews, so a consistently strong rating across that many users is huge news.

### ETravelSim reviews [...] ### Can I get an eSIM for my laptop?

Maybe. No Apple laptops offer this yet, but some that run windows, including Asus, Dell, and HP have eSIM-compatible models.

Nomad eSIM has a comprehensive list here. I reckon Holafly is the best eSIM for any laptop activity since you’ll likely be using up more data, making the unlimited option ideal.

### Are eSIMs cheaper than local SIM cards?

Maybe. Usually, no.

You’re paying for the convenience of not having to faff about with tracking down a local SIM card in every new country or region you visit. However, eSIMs may be cheaper in some destinations with crazy high data prices like Canada and the US.

### Can I top up an eSIM, or do I need to buy a new one?

Maybe. It depends on the provider.

results.content:
In August 2024, I was on a work trip to four countries in Southeast Asia (Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore) so I bought an Airalo regional eSIM card for Asia that was 10GB of data for 30 days for $37. Again, country-specific eSIMs are a better value. For example, my 30-day Japan eSIM was only $24.15 for 30 days for 20GB, which is a much better value for a lower price than my regional Asia eSIM. [...] ### Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam eSIMs

In early 2025, I traveled to Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam using Airalo using country-specific eSIM cards for each place, but they are all covered on Airalo’s regional Asia eSIM plans. First of all, Airalo is the only eSIM company with coverage in Laos from my research. You can buy a Laos-only eSIM (limited options and pricey—$9.50 for 1 GB), and it’s included in the regional Asia eSIM (better value). [...] When I left Singapore, I flew to Japan for a month-long trip and used up the leftover data on my regional Asia eSIM before switching to a Japan-only eSIM. I spent part of my work trip in Japan on a ship traveling around Japan and knew we were going to Busan, Korea for one day so I bought a 5GB regional Asia eSIM ($18.55 for 30 days) to use there. (They also offer cheaper 7-day plans with less data, but I always need to maximize my data so I usually buy the 30-day ones.)

Airalo supplies 30 single‑country data plans that cover the United States, and it also offers 29 multi‑country plans that include the United States as part of a larger package. The available plans range in price from roughly $4.00 to $89.00, and the data caps span from 1 GB to 50 GB, with validity periods of 3 to 365 days. Among the options, 6 plans apply a daily data cap (the amount of data available each day is limited), while 53 plans have a fixed data cap that remains the same regardless of how many days the plan is active.

Summarized by AI, Last updated: Mar 19, 2026

## More eSIM Providers for United States of America

Discover some of the most popular eSIM brands offering plans for United States of America [...] Airalo offers United States of America eSIM plans that include a phone number and the ability to send and receive calls and SMS. The available plans range from 1GB to 50GB of data and cost between $6.00 and $59.00 USD. Validity periods vary from 3 days to 30 days, so users can choose a short‑term or longer‑term option that matches their travel schedule.

All of these plans provide a local United States phone number with the dialing code +1, allow inbound and outbound voice calls, and support both inbound and outbound SMS. Users should review the specific plan details on Airalo’s website and confirm any additional requirements directly with the provider.

### How many data plans does Airalo offer for United States of America? [...] Airalo does not provide a truly unlimited high‑speed data eSIM for the United States of America. The only plans that carry the label “Unlimited” actually offer 3 GB of high‑speed data per day; once that daily allowance is used, the speed is throttled to 1000 kbps. This throttle indicates that the plans are not unlimited in the sense of offering unrestricted high‑speed data.

Instead, Airalo sells fixed‑data plans. For example, a 50 GB plan valid for 30 days costs $42 USD, while a 20 GB plan also valid for 30 days is priced at $37 USD. These fixed‑data options can be more cost‑effective for most travelers, especially those who do not consume large amounts of data every day.

## Planning Your Annual Connectivity Budget

A realistic annual connectivity budget for nomads ranges from $600-2,400, depending on destinations and usage patterns:

   Budget nomad (Southeast Asia focus): $50-80/month
   Balanced nomad (mixed regions): $80-150/month
   Premium nomad (Western Europe/North America): $150-300/month

Remember to factor in setup costs, backup connections, and the occasional expensive emergency top-up when planning your budget.

The catch? Network reliability varies significantly between islands, making backup connectivity essential.

Portugal has become Europe's nomad hub, but connectivity costs reflect Western European standards:

Mexico eSIM plans typically cost $35-50/month, making them competitive for the convenience factor.

United States remains expensive:

results.title: Best eSIM for Europe of 2026 - TechRadar
results.content:
European plans include one-off, monthly, and annual options, and they’re fairly affordable. The cheapest one-off is priced at $2 for 500MB and 2 days, while the cheapest monthly subscription is priced at $8 a month for 5GB/month. The first annual plan is priced at $24 and will get you 24GB or 2GB/month.

Ubigi also has several very interesting features, the main one being smooth data tethering. This means that you’ll be able to share your data without any restrictions, which is perfect if you’re traveling with someone because the other person won’t need to get a Ubigi eSIM.

Speaking of eSIMs, the actual activation is very simple and straightforward, with the service offering a bunch of guides and videos on the official website in case you have any trouble figuring it out. [...] Plans start from just $4.99 for 1GB for 7 days. Other options are 3GB of data for 30 days for $12.49, 5GB of data for 30 days for $19.49, 10GB of data for 30 days for $35.99, 50GB of data for 90 days for $95.99, and 100GB of data for 180 days for $179.99.

The flexible plans are definitely why we recommend Saily to our readers. Whether you're planning a short trip, a euro summer, or planning to move to Europe for a few months, Saily plans have got you covered.

With Saily, you can enable enhanced security features like web protection and ad blockers, making this eSIM one of a kind in the market. Installing your Saily eSIM is a breeze. All you need to do is purchase a plan, download the app, and follow the on-screen instructions for a quick setup. [...] The latter is preferable if you’re not sure about the duration of your trip, while the former is preferable if you know the exact length of your trip and how much data, calling, and SMS allowance you need.

The good news is that there’s no shortage of affordable eSIM packages. You can find an unlimited data package for as low as 15 euros, depending on the validity period. The longer the period, the higher you should expect to pay.

Even if an eSIM package seems expensive at face value, consider that it saves you from potentially steep roaming costs when you travel. It’s not uncommon for people to rack up hundreds of euros in international roaming charges because they used a lot of data, SMS, and calling allowance.
